context_heading: What certified means for accountants in the UK
context: In the UK, the word accountant on its own is not a protected title, so anyone can call themselves an accountant. However, titles such as Chartered Certified Accountant (ACCA), Chartered Accountant (ICAEW, ICAS or Chartered Accountants Ireland) and Chartered Management Accountant (CIMA) are protected, and members must follow their body's ethics, training and complaints rules.

Every accountancy practice must also be supervised for anti-money-laundering purposes, either by a professional body or by HMRC. It is reasonable to ask which body supervises a firm, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance, and how complaints are handled.

questions_heading: Questions to ask a certified accountant
questions: Which professional body gave you your certification, and are you a member in good standing?
Do you hold professional indemnity insurance?
Which body supervises your practice for anti-money-laundering purposes?
How do you handle complaints if I am unhappy with your service?
Do you have experience with businesses like mine?
What information do you need from me to provide a quote?

faqs.q: What does certified mean for an accountant?
faqs.a: Certified usually means the accountant holds a qualification from a professional body, such as ACCA for Chartered Certified Accountants. These qualifications involve training and ethical standards, and members are bound by their body's rules.

faqs.q: How can I check if an accountant is properly qualified?
faqs.a: You can ask which body gave them their qualification and check with that body directly. It is also reasonable to ask about professional indemnity insurance and anti-money-laundering supervision.

faqs.q: Do I need a certified accountant for my small business?
faqs.a: While anyone can call themselves an accountant, using a certified accountant gives you assurance that they have met certain standards. For many small businesses, a certified accountant can handle tax returns, accounts and advice.

faqs.q: What should I have ready when I contact an accountant?
faqs.a: It helps to have your recent financial records, such as bank statements, invoices and receipts, as well as details of your business structure. The accountant can then give you a clearer idea of what they can do for you.

extra_heading: What 'near me' means when you want a certified accountant
extra: Searching for a certified accountant near me suggests you would value being able to meet your accountant face to face, or at least know they are close enough to visit if needed. While much accountancy work can be done remotely, a local accountant can be convenient for dropping off records or having a sit-down review of your accounts. When you enquire, tell us your town or postcode so we can introduce you to a suitable accountant in your area.

Proximity is only one factor. A certified accountant's qualification, experience with your type of business and clear communication matter just as much. You might find that an accountant a little further away is a better fit for your needs, so it is worth asking about how they work and what they specialise in before you decide.

When you compare accountants, ask each one what their quote includes and whether they will handle dealings with HMRC on your behalf. A local accountant can also explain how they prefer to receive your records and how often they will be in touch. Remember that iComply does not provide accountancy services itself; we simply introduce you to a professional who will quote you directly.

extra_faqs.q: Do I have to choose an accountant who is close by?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many people prefer a local accountant for convenience, but others work happily with an accountant further away using phone and email. What matters most is that they are properly qualified and understand your needs.

extra_faqs.q: What should I ask a local accountant at the first meeting?
extra_faqs.a: Ask which professional body gave them their certification, whether they hold professional indemnity insurance and how they handle complaints. It is also sensible to ask about their experience with businesses like yours and what their quote covers.
